findings.text: — §11's "Why" states "two coordinators reported that §3's guard still forces reconnects under load" and cites "power_convertor's sessions saw read_plan, edit_plan, roadmap and crew all answer stale_server_code from mid-afternoon, on a node at load 59–75" with no run id, log path or link, where §1's equivalent report is linked.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §11's "Why" rests on coordinator reports and a load figure that name no run id, log or link, unlike §1's own linked report.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §11's done-when names seven measurable cases and a declared negative control for each, one per case, and the seven controls map one-to-one onto the seven cases.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §11's gate log is the run's own gate log under the node's write paths; no case names a scratchpad or node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §11 names only existing code symbols (`_refuse_when_stale`, `_answer_on_current_code`, `_stale_code_response`, `_SERVE_ON_CURRENT_CODE`, `_CURRENT_CODE_TIMEOUT_S`); no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or version tags reach a symbol or comment.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — §11's stated root cause matches the cited code at every point I checked: `_answer_on_current_code` returns `None` on an unanswered child (`reckon/mcp.py:513-520`) and `_stale_code_response` then replaces the call's own failure (`reckon/mcp.py:571`), with the literal detail "This call failed on the current code too" at `reckon/mcp.py:479`; `_SERVE_ON_CURRENT_CODE` sends every later call of a fallen-back tool to a fresh child first (`reckon/mcp.py:552-554`); each child is one `subprocess.run` bounded at `_CURRENT_CODE_TIMEOUT_S = 120.0` (`reckon/mcp.py:345, 383-396`). The mechanism runs on the real code path: all five registered tools (`read_plan`, `edit_plan`, `roadmap`, `audit`, `crew`) are wrapped by `_refuse_when_stale` (`reckon/mcp.py:2838-2874`), and the `crew` write/read split §11 relies on already exists (`_crew_call_kind` in that registration). §3's own deliverable already names "a child process restarted on a stamp change behind a stable stdio front" as an allowed means, so §11's choice is consistent with, not contrary to, §3.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §11 carries one mechanism ("the guard stops turning slowness into a reconnect") reached through the guard in `reckon/mcp.py`; its clauses are facets of that one repair, not two deliverables.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §11's edge `s11←s9` is declared (`plan-section-depends-on`), s9 is `done`, and the cross-plan ordering §11 relies on is real: `the-crew-surface-is-one-tool-and-a-few-verbs` §5's own followup names `every-plan-write-goes-through-edit-plan#s11` as what it waits on, matching §11's "waits for this section to land".
